preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(l == int(l) and r == int(r) and 1 <= l <= r <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for l, r in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each subsequent line contains two integers l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 10^9) representing the range of cans a customer can buy.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip().upper() in ['YES', 'NO'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive) indicating whether there exists a pack size a such that every customer buying x cans in [l, r] buys more cans than they initially wanted.

postconditions.expression: all((exists(a, 1 <= a <= 10**9) and all((x // a) * a + (a if (x % a) >= (a / 2) else x % a) > x for x in range(l, r + 1))) == (stdout_line.strip().upper() == 'YES') for (l, r), stdout_line in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: For each test case with input range [l, r], the output is 'YES' if and only if there exists an integer a (1 ≤ a ≤ 10^9) such that for every x in [l, r], the total cans bought (packs + remainder or extra pack) is strictly greater than x. The total cans bought is computed as: (x // a) * a + (a if (x % a) >= (a / 2) else x % a).
